Several private fusion companies project grid electricity before 2040: CFS targets ARC grid connection in the early 2030s at ~400 MW in Virginia [c1][c49], and FIA surveys report that over half of companies expect grid power in the early 2030s with over three-quarters by 2039 [c11][c28] — single-source industry optimism. Corroborated institutional voices are more cautious: Senator Manchin called Helion's 2028 claim "almost seems too good to be true" and noted ITER's full operations are slated for 2039 [c47], while DOE's fusion program head described pilot plants as possible "in the 2030s" [c48]. Key technical barriers remain at low readiness: breeding blankets at TRL 3–4 versus the 8–9 needed commercially [c29], tritium extraction systems at low TRL [c32], and no material demonstrated for multiyear fusion neutron damage, tritium retention, and thermal fatigue [c35]. The regulatory pathway is also unclear, with the NRC framework due by end-2027 [c36][c40].

- No green claim quantifies the probability of pre-2040 grid fusion; optimism rests on orange single-source surveys [c11][c28], while breeding blanket, tritium, materials, and regulatory barriers remain unverified at commercial scale [c29][c32][c35][c36].
